title: keycloak-instance values
description: The published interface of this chart. Helm checks these values on lint, template and install, so a caller supplying the wrong shape is told at render time rather than by an operator that accepts the resource and then never reconciles it.

name.description: The name of the Keycloak resource, and the stem every object here is named from. A lower-case DNS subdomain, because it becomes the name of an API object.

image.description: The server build to run. Empty or absent lets the operator choose the one matching its own release, which is the setting that keeps the two matched without anyone maintaining it; null means the same thing, because a caller computing this value has nothing to say when no image is pinned.

service.description: The Service the operator creates. Named here rather than left to default so the route can address it without restating a convention neither of them owns.

port.description: The port the Service exposes and the route's backend addresses. An integer, because both sides of that agreement are ports and neither accepts a string.

hostname.description: The server's own hostname, as a full URL. The scheme is required: the bare form would leave Keycloak resolving scheme and port from request headers on every call, which is the difference between an issuer that is fixed and one that is whatever the last hop claimed.

database.description: The PostgreSQL Keycloak keeps its realm, its users and every session in, and the Secret its credential is read from. There is no state where this is optional - the server does not start without a database.

url.description: A full JDBC URL, because sslmode has no field of its own on the resource. Setting it makes the resource's host, port and database fields ignored, which is why they are not set at all.

secretName.description: The Secret holding both halves of the credential. One Secret and two keys, because the resource takes a key beside each reference.

bootstrapAdmin.description: The first administrator, and the way back in when the realm's configuration is wrong. There are no key names beside it because the operator reads username and password from this Secret by fixed name.

route.description: The one path in. Null renders no HTTPRoute, which is a Keycloak reachable only by port-forward - so both an object and null are valid here, and the null is not an omission to be corrected. Given an object, the hostname and the Gateway are all required together: a route missing any of them is one the API server accepts and no Gateway ever binds.

hostname.description: The DNS name the route matches. A host and only a host - no scheme and no path, because an HTTPRoute hostname is compared against the Host header and nothing else.

gateway.description: The Gateway this route attaches to. It lives in another namespace than the route, which is the ordinary arrangement and the reason the namespace is stated rather than assumed.

sectionName.description: The listener on that Gateway - the ordinary TLS one, since a browser cannot present a client certificate and the mTLS listener is never the right answer for a login page. Null or absent attaches to every listener the Gateway allows, which is the API's own default rather than this chart's.

metrics.description: Whether the cluster has the scrape CRDs and a collector reading them, and the tenant this workload's telemetry belongs to.

enabled.description: Written into spec.serviceMonitor.enabled and never omitted: that field defaults to true, so an unset value on a cluster without the Prometheus operator's CRDs fails the sync. A boolean, because the string "false" is true.

labels.description: The tenant, written onto the Service and onto the pods. Label values are strings, and a number or a boolean written here reaches the API server as the wrong type.
